name: Helping Hands, Loud Voices: Charities and Causes
description: The Red Cross, Oxfam, Amnesty, Greenpeace and the Scouts: how ordinary people built organisations to relieve suffering, defend rights and protect the planet.

checkpoints.name: Early fellowships
checkpoints.note: The Quakers, who appear in England in the 1650s, become known for relief work and campaigns against slavery. In 1844 George Williams and his friends found the YMCA in London to offer young workers a safe place to live and learn.

checkpoints.name: Relief and rules
checkpoints.note: The International Committee of the Red Cross is founded in Geneva in 1863, and the first Geneva Convention follows in 1864 to protect wounded soldiers. The Salvation Army begins in London in 1865, the Nobel Peace Prize is first awarded in 1901, and Scouting begins in 1907.

checkpoints.name: World institutions
checkpoints.note: Alcoholics Anonymous begins in 1935 as a group of people helping each other to stop drinking. Oxfam starts in Oxford in 1942 to send food to people in occupied Greece. The United Nations follows in 1945 and the World Health Organization in 1948.

checkpoints.name: Conscience and nature
checkpoints.note: Jane Goodall begins her study of chimpanzees in Tanzania in 1960. Amnesty International is founded in 1961 to campaign for prisoners of conscience, Rachel Carson's Silent Spring (1962) warns of pesticides, and in 1971 Greenpeace sets out from Vancouver to protest nuclear tests.

checkpoints.name: Concerts and treaties
checkpoints.note: Live Aid in 1985 raises money for famine relief in Ethiopia. The Montreal Protocol (1987) acts against ozone-damaging gases, the IPCC begins in 1988, and the Kyoto Protocol (1997) and Paris Agreement (2015) aim at climate change. Malala Yousafzai wins the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.
